content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) suggests that a target blood glucose level of 16.0 mmol/L can be considered appropriate if it can be achieved without causing hypoglycemia. The ADA endorses the continued use of personal continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) and automated insulin delivery (AID) systems in hospitalized patients when deemed appropriate. However, confirmatory point-of-care glucose measurements should be utilized to guide insulin dosing decisions. The ADA supports the use of SGLT2 inhibitors in hospitalized patients with type 2 diabetes and heart failure. It is recommended that these medications be continued after the patient’s recovery, provided there are no contraindications to their use.
